header: "THROUGH WHOM": when the question asks who issues, approves or sanctions something and the table has a column for it, the key findings must say it too (prompt rule WHO ISSUES, APPROVES OR SANCTIONS). The model sometimes leaves the table to say it alone (the Zero Tolerance answer, 11 Nov 2026: a full "Issued through" column and two findings that never mention it). So I added this plain-code backstop: ONE finding built from the cells of that column, in their own words, and only when the findings do not already name them. Pure: no I/O, no model. Nothing is added when the question does not ask, when there is no such column, or when the findings already say it.

symbols.name: ASKS_WHO
doc: Matches a question that asks who does it: "through whom", "by whom", "who issues / approves / sanctions", "which authority", "issued by".

symbols.name: WHO_COLUMN
doc: Matches the column that holds the answer.

symbols.name: describeIssuers
symbols.sig: export function describeIssuers(table: SynthesisTable | null | undefined, query: string, findings: string[]): { text: string; sources: number[] } | null
doc: Returns one finding that says who issues, built from the table's own column, or null. `findings` are the texts already written: I add nothing when they already name every issuer.

behaviours: a finding is built from the column: who, for how many rows, and that the rest name no one
the two rows are named by their own words
nothing is added when the findings already name the issuer
nothing is added when the question does not ask who
nothing is added when the table has no such column
a column where nothing is named says so, once
and is not said again if the findings already say it
one issuer for every row is said so
several issuers: each one, with its count; more than three rows are counted, not listed
the engine adds it after the checked table, only with room, and the version changed so the stored briefing is made afresh
